observations:
Torah #140 is a single-concept-pair teaching. It contains exactly one bechina domain: the Tzaddik as seal (חותם). The gap analysis found one additional bechina concept ('כל האדם') that attaches naturally to the same existing Package 1 (הַצַּדִּיק וְהַחוֹתָם) — it does not form an independent thematic family.

No second thematic domain of any kind is developed in this teaching. The teaching's sole structural move is:
  [Package 1: good] — The Tzaddik's sealed/total nature
  ↓ via eitza (edge 1271)
  [practical implication: through his disciples one can come to know him]

The eitza edge (אנשיו המקרבין אליו → יוכל להבין מעלת הצדיק) describes a causal mechanism that flows OUT from the package to a practical result, not a new conceptual domain.

There is no evil mirror in Torah #140. The teaching makes no mention of an opposing force, a false tzaddik, or an evil seal. This is consistent with the teaching's brevity and its nature as a positive epistemological reflection on how one approaches the Tzaddik.

All concepts in the source text either:
  (a) belong to Package 1 (צדיק, חותם, and the proposed addition 'כל האדם'), or
  (b) are parable/explanatory elements (wax, inverted letters, disciples as medium) that are eitza-functional rather than bechina-conceptual.

Conclusion: Torah #140 yields exactly 1 package, 2 dataset nodes (plus 1 proposed addition), 0 new packages needed.
